NAV takes some inspiration from Future by likening himself to rockstar Jimi Hendrix, whilst also paying homage to his contemporary. Future has said the nickname comes from him being different in the genre of hip-hop, just as Jimi was in rock, but it’s possible NAV’s usage of the name comes from a different place.

The name “NAV Hendrix” started as a joke on KanyeToThe (KTT), a music discussion forum named after Kanye West. This thread about artists using “Hendrix” as a suffix to their name created a meme on the site. It’s now regularly used on the site, both by both fans and people attempting to troll critics.

“Whitney” likely refers to Whitney Houston, the famous singer known for her drug use who passed away in 2012.

It could be the case that NAV is unaware of the meme and was simply taking notes from Future, but the name “NAV Hendrix” was given to him online before he ever used it himself in a song.

A clever wordplay is established here, linking a meal at Popeyes to a fighting reference.
NAV wants to keep calmness in his community, but he keeps his ‘piece’ just incase, also known as his weapon.

NAV then says he sticks with the drums like Popeyes, which is another reference to weapons. Many automatic weapons have the potential to use drums as their ammunition.



But, also, Popeyes sells ‘drumsticks’, very similar to chicken wings.



So NAV is connecting these two different meanings of drums, being Popeye’s chicken and weapon drums.

After this, he says ‘hit em with a two-piece’ which means that he will use a classic 1-2 fighting combo. This line could also refer to the two-piece chicken meal served at popeyes.

In the next line Nav is alluding to his reluctance to abandon his previous lifestyle despite his new found wealth. He does this through clever wordplay by selecting words that relate to food whilst also having double meanings. The word chicken is used as another word for a kilogram of cocaine. A kilogram of cocaine has a very high street value thus being a metaphor for Nav’s new expensive lifestyle. Nav then reassures the listener by using using the word beef at a metaphor for his old lifestyle. The word beef is frequently used to describe a conflict between people. Thus meaning that despite Nav’s new lifestyle he hasn’t changed and will continue to cause conflict with people who he sees fit. Also, the money hasn’t made him soft.

NAV made his break into the mainstream after producing 2015’s “Back to Back” by Drake, who he has previously credited for helping him take off after the fellow Toronto native played his song, “The Man,” on OVO Sound Radio. Along with “Back to Back,” NAV has gone on to produce Travis Scott’s “beibs in the trap” from 2016 and Gucci Mane’s “Curve,” released the following year.

NAV—who doesn’t have a producer tag on his beats—expresses his distaste for whenever a producer decides to insert their catchphrase or calling card on an instrumental, perhaps because it may distract from the content of the song. meaning:
NAV is saying he’s with a beautiful, desirable woman — a “bad lil’ vibe” — and her presence brings him emotional relief or distraction from the pain he’s feeling. This fits the recurring theme of using relationships (or situationships) as a coping mechanism, where the person might not solve his problems but temporarily makes him feel better. It also suggests a level of dependency: he’s relying on her to manage what he’s going through.

There’s also a possible double meaning:

She’s attractive and brings him pleasure,

But she also represents emotional medicine, like in the earlier metaphors (therapy, novocaine, etc.).

Here NAV is expressing something deeper and more existential: no matter how he feels — whether he’s high or low, up or down — the pain never fully disappears. Even when he’s with someone who makes him feel good, or when life seems alright, that underlying emptiness or sadness still lingers. It’s a confession of emotional numbness or permanence of pain, where even happiness doesn’t erase the struggle.

line: I’ma fuck the game up when I drop “Bag”

meaning:
“Bag” was a fan-favorite unreleased track by NAV that he first previewed back in 2016. For a long time, it never saw a release, and fans had since questioned NAV over the years about dropping it. NAV addressed this in an interview with Tim Westwood in August 2019, suggesting he might drop the track on Audiomack as a non-album gift. On May 4, 2020, four days before the release of “Run It Up” and Good Intentions, NAV’s manager Cash, dropped the track on his Audiomack. The tracker later found a home on the deluxe version of the album.

It’s worth noting that a similar thing has happened before to NAV with the song “Habits,” which was first previewed in 2015 before finally being released on the deluxe version of NAV’s sophomore studio album, Bad Habits in March 2019 after similar questioning from fans.

line: I don’t wanna ever wake up (Wake up)

line: You know I ain’t sleep, girl, you see me callin’ (And you see me callin’) I just hope you catch me when you see me fallin’ (Fallin’)

meaning:
“You know I ain’t sleep, girl, you see me callin' (And you see me callin')”
NAV is reaching out late at night, unable to sleep, clearly going through something emotional or mental. He’s trying to connect with someone — likely a woman he cares about — and pointing out that she knows he’s awake and struggling. There’s a sense of desperation here: he’s not hiding his pain, and she sees it. The repetition emphasizes that he’s making a real effort to get through to her, and her lack of response might be making things worse.

“I just hope you catch me when you see me fallin' (Fallin')”
This line is a metaphor for emotional vulnerability and dependence. NAV is confessing that he’s not in a good place — he’s “falling,” whether that’s into depression, anxiety, bad habits, or emotional breakdown. He hopes that the person he’s calling will be there for him, to support him or save him before he hits rock bottom. It’s a rare moment of openness, asking for help in a subtle but sincere way.

line: When everybody sleep, I’m up When everybody sleep, I’m up Baby, can you wait up for me? When everybody sleep, I’m up You see me callin’ you (Wait up, wait) When everybody sleep, I’m up (Wait up, wait, wait up, wait) When everybody sleep, I’m up (Wait up, wait)

NAV is saying that when everyone is asleep, he is the one that is awake.
This line reflects both NAV’s insomnia and his mindset as a late-night thinker and hustler. While others are sleeping — either literally or metaphorically — NAV is wide awake, battling his thoughts, chasing success, or dealing with the emotional weight of his lifestyle. The phrase suggests a sense of isolation; even with fame and money, NAV feels alone, stuck in his own head while the rest of the world rests.

There’s also a flex in the statement — he’s grinding when others are resting, a classic theme in rap that signals dedication and ambition.
